done.why: I came to find treasure and keep it safe. The platinum bar and the painting are both locked in the trophy case and the game counted them as my collection, so I stopped there happy, at 65 points and Novice Adventurer.

about: A white house with a trophy case that's waiting to be filled, sitting on top of a big underground world. You go down, fight a troll, learn the quirks of strange rooms like the one that echoes and the mirror that moves you, and work out how to get your finds back up to the surface. That part is hard because the trap door gets barred behind you and the chimney only lets you carry a little.

ending.what: My own goal: two treasures (a painting and a platinum bar) locked in the trophy case, score 65 of 350. It isn't the end of the whole game.

moments.note: "can I go into the house?" got back 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.'
'climb through the window' just worked, the way I'd say it.
The trophy case 'expects to be filled.' That told me where treasure belongs.
The trap door slammed and got barred behind me. Trapped.
I greeted the troll, he bowed, and then it said 'You can't see any such thing.' Mixed signals.
Beat the troll in two swings and he vanished in black fog.
Trying to take the bar just echoed 'Bar bar ...' back at me.
I said 'echo' on a hunch, the room changed, and I got the bar.
Touching the mirror made the room rumble and I was somewhere else, but the room looked exactly the same.
Went in circles around the mirror rooms, twisting passage and cave. A thief walked by and found 'nothing of value' even though I was carrying a platinum bar.
'push open the trap door' said I couldn't see it, but 'open the trap door' knew what it was.
Couldn't take the painting because my load was too heavy. I had to drop stuff.
The chimney told me exactly what I could take up: me, my lamp and one thing. Very clear.
'drop everything except the lantern and the painting' wasn't understood.
Went back down and the trap door got barred again. I had to use the chimney twice.
The Living Room listed 'Your collection of treasures' the moment I walked in.
'how am I doing?' was understood and gave me a score and a rank.

wished: Ask questions like 'can I go into the house?' or 'which ways are open?' and get an answer
Say 'drop everything except the lantern' instead of listing every item
Keep the trap door open so I didn't have to climb the chimney twice
Talk with the troll, since he bowed to me
Some way to tell the two identical-looking Mirror Rooms apart

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: The only hint about what the trophy case was for, and it set my goal.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: A real shock. Who barred it? From then on, getting out was the problem.
Funny and confusing at once, and it got me thinking about sound.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: Clear, fair rule that shaped my whole plan of ferrying one treasure at a time.

lines.line: A "lean and hungry" gentleman just wandered through, carrying a large bag. Finding nothing of value, he left disgruntled.
lines.why: Made me worry for my treasures and want to get them home quickly.

fun.why: Killing the troll, the echo trick and working out the chimney ferry were all satisfying. Seeing my collection listed felt like a reward.

engagement.why: Being trapped gave me a clear reason to keep going, and the thief made me hurry. The looping around the mirror rooms dragged a little.

difficulty.why: The puzzles I hit were fair. Some of my natural wording was rejected, and the barred door doubled the work, but nothing stopped me for long.

interestingness.why: Rooms with their own rules (echo, mirror, a chimney with a size limit) made the place feel alive and strange.

prose.why: Vivid, often witty descriptions, like the vandals 'with exceptional taste' and the case's 'patient air'. Revisited rooms show only their name, which made it harder to tell where I was.
